pages.text:
QUANT FINANCE
FACTOR ZOO
A research map for asset-pricing models, anomalies and investable tests.

FACTORS
Factor vs Alpha
Trait → sort → return
TRAIT
HML
SIGNAL
ALPHA
From firm attribute to model residual
FACTOR
A characteristic is an observable trait. Sorting creates factor returns such as HML; a signal ranks stocks. Alpha is the regression intercept left after the chosen model, which also determines whether a return pattern is anomalous.
Models can absorb yesterday’s anomaly; what survives depends on the benchmark.

ANOMALY
Anomaly Is Relative
An anomaly is benchmark-dependent: specify the model before calling a return pattern unexplained. Tests against broader model sets ask whether the premium survives controls.

Characteristic
An observable firm trait, such as book-to-market.

Factor return
A return series formed by sorting stocks on a characteristic, such as HML.

Signal
A cross-sectional score ranks stocks for portfolio construction.

Unexplained
A pattern the selected benchmark model fails to explain.

Alpha
The regression intercept left unexplained by chosen factors.

Model-relative
Expanded benchmarks can absorb yesterday’s anomaly exposures.

CAPM
CAPM Prices Beta

1
Pricing rule
CAPM makes expected excess return proportional to market beta times the market risk premium; its Security Market Line is linear under the model assumptions.

2
Beta
Beta is covariance with the market divided by market-return variance; only systematic risk is priced. Two-fund separation gives all investors the same risky mix; market clearing makes it the market portfolio.

3
Equilibrium
w_mkt ∝ Σ⁻¹(μ − r_f1); μ − r_f1 ∝ Σw_mkt.

pages.title: CAPM Limits
pages.text:
CAPM Limits
Flat SML

LOW BETA

SIZE / VALUE
The empirical SML was flatter than CAPM predicts; BAB formalizes the low-beta pattern. Size and value returns exceeded beta-only predictions. These failures did not kill factor-based asset pricing; research shifted to multifactor models.




ROLL (1977)
The true market spans unobservable bonds, real estate and human capital; equity-only CAPM tests are limited. This shifted research toward multifactor models.

MODELS
Model Lineage
Models broaden the benchmark from market risk to characteristic-based returns, investment, profitability and mispricing. Each extension absorbs patterns, but fit depends on factor construction, assumptions and model selection.

CAPM
CAPM links expected excess returns to market beta under a mean-variance efficient market portfolio and homogeneous expectations.

APT
APT assumes a linear factor structure and no-arbitrage, without specifying the factors’ economic identities.

FF3
Adds size (SMB) and value (HML) to market beta after CAPM leaves those return patterns unexplained.

Carhart
Adds a winner-minus-loser momentum return because momentum-sorted portfolios retain alpha against FF3.

FF5 / q
FF5 adds profitability and investment; q uses investment-to-assets and return on equity.

SY / q5
Mispricing clusters and expected growth broaden fit; selection still matters.

FF3
Fama–French 3
Annual 2×3
MKT
SMB
HML
2×3
Three spreads; six portfolios
SORT
Each June, split size at the NYSE median and book-to-market at the 30th/70th percentiles. The independent sorts form six value-weighted portfolios; SMB contrasts small with big, while HML contrasts high with low book-to-market.
Independent sorts separate size and value exposures.

MOMENTUM
Carhart MOM
Monthly rebalanced, value-weighted UMD adds winners-minus-losers to FF3; fund attribution links apparent manager skill to momentum. Rank t−12 to t−2 returns, skip the latest month, and form within-size 2×3 long-short 30%/decile spreads. Rebounds can crash momentum. r_i-r_f = α_i+β_iMKT+s_iSMB+h_iHML+m_iUMD+ε_i.
UMD
LONG WINNER LEG
Top minus bottom 30% or decile; within-size 2×3.
RANK
t−12/t−2
Skip the most recent month.
RISK
MOMENTUM CRASHES
Rebounds can cause crashes.
ATTR
Fund attribution
Skill reduces to passive tilt

FF5
FF5 Adds RMW + CMA
RMW + CMA



RMW
Robust-minus-weak profitability adds operating profitability to the market, size and value factors; it captures differences in firms’ operating strength.


CMA
Conservative-minus-aggressive investment adds an investment dimension, motivated by dividend-discount logic and firms’ investment behavior.


HML
HML can be partly redundant in some samples; its marginal role depends on the test assets and remains debated.
Dividend-discount rationale; sample-dependent HML
FF5 adds profitability (RMW) and investment (CMA). Broader fit is not a universal verdict; HML may be partly redundant in some samples.

pages.title: q and q5 Models
pages.text:
q and q5 Models
Production

I/A + ROE

q5 + EG
The q model uses market, investment-to-assets (I/A) and return on equity (ROE), linking expected returns to investment and profitability. q5 adds expected growth (EG); independent size, investment and profitability sorts form 27 portfolios.




Trade-off
Greater structure still leaves results dependent on sample and construction choices.

SY MODEL
MGMT + PERF

1
MGMT
MGMT clusters investment and accrual anomalies into a composite mispricing factor; its design summarizes related characteristics rather than treating each signal as independent.

2
PERF
PERF groups profitability and momentum patterns. Together, MGMT and PERF summarize 11 known anomaly characteristics in the Stambaugh–Yuan framework.

3
Post-hoc caveat
Its horse-race advantage needs caution because construction is post hoc.

TESTS
Testing Models
Different tests answer different pricing questions; the test assets and covariance estimates shape the verdict. Regression fit alone does not settle the economic explanation.

Time series
Regress portfolio returns on factor returns; inspect the intercept.

Cross section
Ask whether betas or traits explain average-return differences.

GRS
Jointly test whether test-portfolio alphas equal zero.

Test assets
Changing the portfolios can change the model comparison.

Covariance
GRS depends on estimated residual covariance across portfolios.

Inference
No single regression settles the economic explanation.

PREMIA
Premia Stories
Risk compensation, behavioral mispricing and limits to arbitrage compete; a factor may mix them. Risk pays for bad-state exposure. Behavioral errors include overreaction, underreaction and extrapolation. Trading frictions delay correction, while value, momentum, low-volatility and size each have failure stories.
RISK
BAD-STATE LOSSES
Pays for losses in adverse states.
BEHV
Behavior
Overreaction, underreaction and extrapolation move prices.
FRIC
SHORTING LIMITS
Shorting limits slow correction.
MIX
Stories overlap
Competing stories can overlap

ZOO
Multiple Testing
Trials raise false-discovery risk



ALIASES
Several labels may reflect one latent exposure rather than distinct sources of return; correlated definitions can repackage a signal.


ABSORBED
A broader benchmark can explain an anomaly that appeared under CAPM or FF3, changing the residual claim.


SELECTION
Many trials make a t-stat above 2 weak evidence; require a rationale, point-in-time data, robustness and independent confirmation.
Net costs can erase a premium
Trading costs may erase the premium. Test incremental value against known factors, model realistic implementation and record the full search process.

SCORE
Factor Scorecard
No factor story is a verdict; each one needs a failure test.
VALUE
MOMENTUM
QUALITY
LOW RISK
Risk, mispricing and mining
TEST
Value mixes distress/duration risk and extrapolation; metric choice creates a mining risk. Momentum carries crash exposure, underreaction stories and parameter-search risk. Quality and investment pair cash-flow or q-theory stories with definition choices.
Low volatility, size and liquidity face leverage, funding, sector and trading-friction confounds.

FAMILIES
Factor Families
Each factor family needs controls suited to its signal, data source and likely confounds. Families can overlap, but their measurement risks differ.

Value
B/P, E/P and EBIT/EV; control industry, profitability and leverage.

Momentum
12–1, residual and earnings signals; test reversal and crash exposure.

Quality
GP/A, ROE and accruals; control sector, leverage and size.

Investment
Asset growth, capex growth and net issuance; check profitability.

Risk / liq.
Beta, volatility and spreads/turnover; control sector, leverage, size and price.

Sentiment / alt.
Revisions, short interest, news and web data require coverage and timestamp controls.

PORTFOLIO
Portfolio Forms

1
Long-short
Decile or rank-weighted dollar-neutral portfolios test the premium; a long-only benchmark tilt tests constrained stock selection.

2
Optimizer
Residualized signals fit constrained optimizers; factor-mimicking portfolios serve risk models. Report weighting, rebalancing frequency, breakpoint universe, sector and beta neutrality, leverage, and cost assumptions.

3
Report design
必须报告构建选择：加权方式、调仓频率、断点股票池、行业中性、贝塔中性、杠杆和成本假设。

pages.title: Timing & Crowding
pages.text:
Timing & Crowding
Timing

Spreads

Crowding
Valuation spreads, recent factor returns, macro regimes and volatility may inform timing, but they add another layer of multiple testing. Crowded factors can persist until liquidity disappears, then unwind sharply.




Monitor
Track flows, common holdings, short interest, borrow, turnover and manager correlation.

A-SHR
U.S. vs A-Shares
Market transfer
MOM
SIZE
QUALITY
STRUCT.
Re-test, do not transplant
CHECK
US momentum is canonical; A-share momentum is more horizon- and limit-event-dependent. Quality screens must watch subsidies, related parties and earnings management. 美股动量是经典稳健因子，而 A 股动量更依赖期限和涨跌停事件；A 股规模因子受壳价值和量化拥挤塑造；A 股质量筛选必须更关注补贴、关联方活动和盈余管理动机。
Shell value and quant crowding have shaped A-share size behavior.

SORT
The 2×3 Sort
Independent sorts



SIZE
Split the universe into small and big by market capitalization; independently sort the chosen characteristic into low, middle and high buckets.


INTERSECT
Cross the two rankings to form six portfolios; compare high with low within each size group.


HML
HML averages the high-characteristic portfolios and subtracts the low-characteristic average across size buckets.
HML = ½(SmallHigh + BigHigh) − ½(SmallLow + BigLow). Higher characteristic returns minus lower, averaged across size.；A Fama-French-style 2×3 sort works as follows: split the universe into small/big by market cap, split the characteristic into low/mid/high by breakpoints, then form six portfolios.
Independent sorting keeps the characteristic spread from merely proxying for firm size; the same template applies to profitability or investment.

STRAT
Strategy Path
A factor is not yet a strategy: define the universe, forecast, portfolio, execution, risk limits, capacity, monitoring and governance. Test rationale and incremental value, include costs, red-team the result, paper-trade, then consider a small live allocation.
PLAN
INVESTABLE UNIV
Define investable names and forecasts.
TEST
Robust
Check incrementality, costs and capacity.
RISK
SET RISK LIMITS
Set limits and monitor drawdowns.
LIVE
PAPER-TRADE FIRST
before live allocation

pages.title: Factor Checklist
pages.text:
Factor Checklist



1
TIMESTAMP
Evidence & rationale
THEORY：A priori case
DATA：Point-in-time
NEUTRAL：Control exposures
UNIQUE：Incremental value


2
NO-LEAK
Robustness
METHOD：Conservative tests
IC：Sorts agree
HORIZON：Reasonable range
UNIVERSE：Broader samples


3
NET COST
Tradability
COSTS：Cost realism
TURNOVER：Realistic rates
BORROW：Available names
CAPACITY：Enough liquidity


4
GOVERN
Library & warning
FAILURE：False discoveries
MONITOR：Track live risk
OWNER：Assign review
REGIME：Stay humble

TUTORIAL 04 · PART II THEORY
THE FACTOR ZOO
因子动物园 — Theory and Taxonomy of Equity Factors. Every subsequent factor tutorial drills into one family; this one builds the asset-pricing lineage, the taxonomy, the "why do factors earn premia" debate, and the sober statistical reality of the factor zoo.

SECTION 1–2
WHAT IS A FACTOR? 什么是因子？
A factor in equity research is a systematic, cross-sectionally observable characteristic — or return series constructed from such a characteristic — that explains differences in expected returns across stocks. If we write the return-generating process as:
then    is a factor return,    is the stock's loading, and    is idiosyncratic noise. A factor is useful if it reduces the covariance matrix to a low-rank-plus-diagonal structure and/or commands a non-zero risk premium       .
Critical epistemic point: "Anomaly" is model-relative, not absolute. As benchmark models expand (CAPM → FF3 → Carhart4 → FF5 → FF6), yesterday's anomaly becomes today's risk factor.

CHARACTERISTIC 特征
A firm-level observable at time   — e.g. book-to-market ratio     

FACTOR 因子
A return series (usually long-short) built by sorting stocks on a characteristic — e.g. HML

ANOMALY 异象
An empirical pattern a benchmark model fails to explain — model-relative, not absolute

ALPHA Α 阿尔法
The intercept in a factor-model regression: return unexplained by the chosen factors
Risk factors earn premia as compensation for bad-state exposure; mispricing factors capture the slow correction of behavioral or friction-driven price deviations — most documented factors are argued to be some mixture of both.

SECTION 2
THEORETICAL LINEAGE 理论谱系



CAPM (1964–66)
Sharpe, Lintner, Mossin. One factor: market beta. The Security Market Line predicts every asset lies on             . Empirically rejected: flat SML, size effect, value effect, Roll's critique.


APT (ROSS 1976)
Drops mean-variance machinery; assumes linear factor structure plus no-arbitrage. Justifies "find   common factors" empirically without requiring utility maximization. Expected returns are approximately linear in factor loadings:           .


FF3 (1993)
MKT + SMB (size) + HML (value). 2×3 independent sort: NYSE median size breakpoint; 30th/70th B/M breakpoints. Dramatically improved cross-section fit but could not explain momentum.


CARHART 4 (1997)
FF3 + UMD (12-1 momentum, skipping last month). Rebalanced monthly — reflecting momentum's short signal half-life. Became the standard academic benchmark for a decade.


FF5 (2015) & Q-FACTOR (HXZ 2015)
FF5 adds RMW (profitability) + CMA (investment), motivated by dividend-discount-model decomposition — HML becomes largely redundant. q-factor derives same premia from production-side q-theory: ME, I/A, ROE. Two independent routes converging validates the profitability/investment premium.

SECTION 3–4
GRS TEST & WHY FACTORS EARN PREMIA 检验与溢价来源

1
TIME-SERIES VS. CROSS-SECTIONAL TESTS
Time-series regressions test whether a portfolio's alpha is zero given factors:              . The GRS test asks whether all test-asset alphas are jointly zero — preventing one pretty alpha from hiding broad model failure. Sensitive to test-asset choice; one diagnostic, not a final verdict. 防止单一漂亮阿尔法掩盖模型普遍失败。

2
RISK COMPENSATION 风险补偿
Exposure to factor   raises the volatility of consumption/wealth in bad states (recessions, liquidity crunches, tail events). The premium     is demanded by rational, risk-averse investors — permanent because bearing the risk is unavoidable in equilibrium.

3
BEHAVIORAL MISPRICING 行为错误定价
Prices deviate from fundamental value due to investor psychology (overreaction, underreaction, extrapolation, lottery preference) or market frictions (limits to arbitrage, shorting costs, funding constraints). Premia can erode as more capital chases them or as trading costs rise. 原则上可被套利消除。
No serious practitioner needs a factor to belong purely to one camp. What matters: does the story predict when the factor should fail? Value fails when distress risk is realized; momentum crashes at sharp rebounds; low volatility suffers when leverage constraints relax.

SECTION 5
THE FACTOR ZOO PROBLEM 因子动物园问题
Scale of the Problem 问题规模
400+
Hundreds of published anomalies cannot all be independent sources of expected return. Some are aliases for the same latent exposure, some are subsumed by known factors, some are too expensive to trade, and some are false discoveries produced by multiple testing on the same finite dataset. 数百个已发表异象不可能都是独立预期收益来源。
The number of factors that "survive against an expanding set of controls" is far smaller than the number "in the literature." A t-stat of 2.0 that was once the publication threshold implies a false-discovery rate of roughly 50% under realistic multiple-testing conditions.
REDUNDANCY 冗余
Many claimed factors are linear combinations of MKT, SMB, HML, UMD — correlated aliases that add no independent pricing information.
DATA MINING 数据挖掘
Thousands of characteristics tried on the same US equity sample. Even random characteristics pass a t>2 filter with high frequency given enough tries.
MULTIPLE-TESTING DISCIPLINE 多重检验纪律
Harvey, Liu & Zhu (2016): adjust thresholds upward (t > 3.0 for new factors). Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control. Out-of-sample and international replication are the gold standards.
MINIMUM STANDARD 最低标准
Economic rationale · point-in-time construction · robustness across periods and universes · low correlation to existing factors · implementable net of costs · multiple-testing-aware validation.

SECTIONS 6–7
FACTOR TAXONOMY & SCORECARD 因子分类与评分卡
MASTER TAXONOMY 分类总表
Family 族 | Representative Signals 代表信号
Value 价值 | B/P, E/P, EBIT/EV, CFO/P
Momentum 动量 | 12-1 return, residual mom, earnings mom
Quality 质量 | GP/A, ROE, accruals, F-score, QMJ
Investment 投资 | Asset growth, capex growth, net issuance
Low Risk 低风险 | Beta, idio-vol, downside vol
Liquidity 流动性 | Amihud, turnover, spread, ADV
Sentiment 情绪 | Analyst revisions, short interest, news tone
Alt Data 另类数据 | Web traffic, app usage, supply chain text








RISK VS. MISPRICING SCORECARD 逐因子评分
Factor | Risk Story | Behavioral Story
Value | Distress & duration risk | Extrapolation, overreaction
Momentum | Crash & optionality exposure | Underreaction, slow diffusion
Quality | Defensive cash flows | Underappreciated persistence
Investment | q-theory investment risk | Overinvestment, empire building
Low Vol | Leverage constraints (BAB) | Lottery demand for high beta
Size | Illiquidity / funding risk | Neglected firms






The scorecard is not a verdict — it is a prompt. For every factor, write down what evidence would convince you it is not real.

SECTIONS 8–9
CONSTRUCTION STYLES & FACTOR TIMING 构建方式与因子择时

LONG-SHORT ACADEMIC FACTOR
Decile or 2×3 sort; value-weighted; tests whether the premium exists in principle. Reports pure factor return. Not directly investable due to shorting costs, turnover, and capacity.

RANK-WEIGHTED DOLLAR-NEUTRAL
Weights proportional to cross-sectional rank; dollar-neutral by construction; smoother exposure than decile sorts; still requires shorting but reduces turnover concentration.

LONG-ONLY BENCHMARK TILT
Factor expressed as overweights/underweights vs. a benchmark. Tests benchmark-relative stock selection under real constraints. Always report: weighting, rebalancing frequency, breakpoint universe, sector/beta neutrality.

FACTOR TIMING & CROWDING 择时与拥挤
Valuation spreads, macro regimes, crowding indicators can contain information — but add another layer of multiple testing. Safer default: diversification across factors with drawdown-aware risk budgeting. Monitor common-manager holdings, ETF flows, short interest, borrow cost, turnover spikes.

SECTIONS 10–11
US VS A-SHARES & THE 2×3 SORT 美股与A股 · 算例
FACTORS IN US VS A-SHARES 市场差异
MARKET STRUCTURE 市场结构
A-share shorting constraints are more severe; limit-up/limit-down events distort momentum signals; disclosure quality and earnings-management incentives differ significantly from US markets.
MOMENTUM 动量
US momentum is a robust canonical factor. A-share momentum is more horizon- and limit-event-dependent — treat any cross-market factor import as a hypothesis, not a parameter-free truth.
SIZE & QUALITY A股规模/质量
A-share size has been shaped by shell value and quant crowding. Quality screens must be more alert to subsidies, related-party activity, and earnings-management incentives unique to the A-share regulatory regime.
WORKED EXAMPLE: THE 2×3 SORT 算例
A Fama-French-style 2×3 sort on a toy universe works as follows:
COMPUTE HML FACTOR
FORM 2×3 PORTFOLIOS
RANK CHARACTERISTIC
SPLIT BY SIZE
Independent sorting keeps the two dimensions near-orthogonal by construction. The same template applies to profitability, investment, and custom factors. Always use NYSE breakpoints (not the full universe) to avoid microcap domination of the sort breakpoints.

pages.title: FROM FACTORS TO STRATEGIES 从因子到策略
pages.text:
FROM FACTORS TO STRATEGIES 从因子到策略



1
ECONOMIC RATIONALE & SIGNAL 经济逻辑与信号
Steps 1–2
Articulate the theoretical reason before seeing the backtest
Build a clean, point-in-time signal with no look-ahead
Confirm IC, sorts, and regressions agree directionally


2
SINGLE-FACTOR & INCREMENTALITY TESTS 单因子与增量检验
Steps 3–4
Single-factor sort across reasonable horizons and universes
Incrementality vs. known factors (FF5, q5, Carhart)
Apply multiple-testing-aware thresholds (t > 3.0)


3
BACKTEST & RED TEAM 回测与红队
Steps 5–6
Walk-forward or out-of-sample evaluation
Red-team stress: different universes, sub-periods, geographies
Cost and turnover realism — borrow cost, market impact


4
CONSTRAINED PORTFOLIO → LIVE 约束组合到实盘
Steps 7–9
Constrained portfolio construction with universe rules and risk limits
Paper trade with full execution assumptions and capacity estimates
Small live allocation with monitoring and failure-scenario governance

SECTIONS 13–14
PRACTICAL CHECKLIST & SUMMARY 实践清单与小结
WHAT MAKES A GOOD FACTOR 好因子的标准
It is known at the time it is used — no look-ahead, point-in-time construction 使用时确实已知
It has a reason to exist before seeing the backtest — theory first 在看到回测前就有存在理由
It survives neutralization to obvious exposures (sector, size, beta) 对明显暴露中性化后仍存在
IC, portfolio sorts, and regressions agree directionally IC、分层和回归方向一致
It works across reasonable horizons and universes — not just US large-cap 1990–2020 跨期限和股票池稳健
It is not just a renamed existing factor — passes incrementality tests 不是已有因子的改名
It survives costs, turnover, and capacity — t-stat net of friction 能扛住成本和换手
It has a failure story and a monitoring plan 有失效故事和监控方案
MODEL LINEAGE SUMMARY 模型谱系汇总
Model | Year | Factors # | Grounding
CAPM | 1964 | 1 | Mean-variance equilibrium
APT | 1976 | K | No-arbitrage, linear factors
FF3 | 1993 | 3 | Empirical + risk rationalization
Carhart 4 | 1997 | 4 | Empirical momentum add-on
FF5 | 2015 | 5 | Dividend-discount decomposition
q (HXZ) | 2015 | 4 | Investment-based q-theory
q5 | 2021 | 5 | q-theory + expected growth
Stambaugh-Yuan | 2017 | 4 | Behavioral mispricing clusters








The factor zoo is both a library and a warning. Good factor research combines theory, data discipline, conservative testing, cost realism, and humility about regimes. 因子动物园既是资料库，也是警告。

limitations: Token overlap is not semantic entailment
Visible content units count substantive paragraphs and table rows, not model-evaluated meaning
AIMate provenance identifies typed objects; reference structures without provenance require visual review, so their structure recall is a lower bound
Bilingual distribution, whitespace and table text extraction differ across producers
A zero short-paragraph fragmentation score does not exclude conceptual over-fragmentation; inspect planner and per-page evidence
